translationRepairs: His great-grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously titled Empress Mingzhen.
His great-great-grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously titled Empress Mingzhen.
高祖母 follows 四代祖湍 and precedes 曾祖昂, so she is the fourth-generation ancestress (great-great-grandmother), not the great-grandmother.
The Gaozu's great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.
His great-great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.
高祖母 is the kinship term great-great-grandmother, not “Gaozu’s” mother or grandmother; the generation must be corrected without treating 高祖 as a personal title.

After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stationed at the Northern Capital as military governor; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.

After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
北京留守 is a capital stay-behind post, not a military governorship; “prefect” is also wrong, since 留守 is not 刺史.
The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang. Pointing at the future emperor, he told Gaozu, "This commander is very caola—without grave cause do not cast him aside."
The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang. Pointing at the future emperor, he told Gaozu, "This commander is very fierce and capable—without grave cause do not cast him aside."
操剌 is vernacular praise meaning fierce and capable; leaving it as untranslated “caola” is not English and hides the Khitan ruler’s assessment.
In the third month of the fifth year he was made military governor of the Ye capital and retained command of the palace guard horse and foot.
In the third month of the fifth year he was made stay-behind governor of the Ye capital and concurrently commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot.
鄴都留守 is a stay-behind post, and 兼 marks a concurrent palace-guard command, not a military governorship he merely retained.
In the third month of the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of the Ye capital while also serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard's cavalry and infantry.
In the third month of the fifth year he was transferred to stay-behind governor of the Ye capital while also serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard's cavalry and infantry.
The literal line repeats the same office error: 鄴都留守 is not 節度使.
In the seventh month of the sixth year he was made military governor of the Northern Capital and commissioner of the Hedong circuit.
In the seventh month of the sixth year he was made stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
The Chinese pairs two distinct offices: 北京留守 and 河東節度使; only the latter is a military commissionership.
In the seventh month of the sixth year he was appointed military governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
In the seventh month of the sixth year he was appointed stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong.
Literal English likewise renders 北京留守 as a military governorship, which the source does not say.
In the first month of 944 the Khitan invaded the south; their ruler marched a great host to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei through Yanmen Pass.
In the first month of 944 the Khitan invaded the south; their ruler marched a great host to Chanzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei through Yanmen Pass.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Chunzhou is a false romanization of a different character.
In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitan marched south; the Khitan ruler led a great army straight to Chunzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei to lead troops into Yanmen.
In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitan marched south; the Khitan ruler led a great army straight to Chanzhou and sent the tribal general Prince Wei to lead troops into Yanmen.
The same 澶州 error appears in the literal rendering.
On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor Liu Yuan and his deputy; Hui declared himself acting military governor.
On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui declared himself acting military governor.
殺契丹監軍及副使劉願 names Liu Yuan with both titles; the original invents a second unnamed deputy, and later units mention only 願.
The Khitan then appointed Hui military governor of Shaan, Hou Zhang commander of local horse and foot, and Wang Yan his deputy, but they refused the orders.
The Khitan then appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander, but they refused the orders.
陜州兵馬留後 is an acting command of Shaanzhou’s forces, not a full 節度使; the other two titles are likewise more specific in the Chinese.
The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander and patrol commissioner, and sent Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉

The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉
The original omits 本城, 內外巡檢使兼都虞候, and 其子; 都虞候 is a disciplinary command, not a registrar.

The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief registrar, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉

The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉
都虞候 is the army’s chief disciplinary officer, not a registrar.
On guiwei the bandit Wang Qiong of Chunzhou cut the pontoon bridge with his followers; Qiong was defeated and killed.
On guiwei the bandit Wang Qiong of Chanzhou cut the pontoon bridge with his followers; Qiong was defeated and killed.
澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.
On the day guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chunzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.
On the day guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chanzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.
The literal line repeats Chunzhou for 澶州.
The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lang'e military governor of Chunzhou; greedy and brutal, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.
The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; greedy and brutal, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.
朗鄂 was made 澶州節度使; the prefecture is Chanzhou.
At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lang'e military governor of Chunzhou; Lang'e was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.
At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; Lang'e was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.
Literal English again misromanizes 澶州 as Chunzhou.
On New Year's Day of the third month an edict remitted all miscellaneous levies in Hedong beyond the established taxes.
On the first day of the third month an edict remitted all miscellaneous levies in Hedong beyond the established taxes.
三月丙戌朔 is the first day of the third month, not New Year’s Day, which would be the first of the first month.

On the day gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry and Defender of Sizhou and Acting Grand Guardian, Grand Guardian of Taiyuan and Acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief registrar of the Northern Capital's horse and foot, Defender of Zhengzhou and Acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Northern Capital's Xingjie army, Prefect of Chenzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie army, Prefect of Shanzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning army, Prefect of Suizhou.

On the day gengxu the Emperor appointed Liu Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry, Defender of Sizhou and Acting Grand Guardian, Yin of Taiyuan and Acting Grand Marshal; Guo Congyi, chief registrar of the Northern Capital's horse and foot, Defender of Zhengzhou and Acting Grand Guardian; Li Hongxin, commander of the left wing of the Northern Capital's Xingjie army, Prefect of Chenzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Shang Hongqian, commander of the right wing of the Xingjie army, Prefect of Shanzhou and Acting Minister of Works; Gai Wan, commander of the left wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Caizhou; Zhou Hui, commander of the right wing of the Wujie army, Prefect of Puzhou; and Zhu Fengqian, commander of the Baoning army, Prefect of Suizhou.
劉崇 was appointed 太原尹, the Yin of Taiyuan, not Grand Guardian of Taiyuan; 檢校太保 is a prior acting rank.
Shi Hongzhao was made military governor of Xuzhou and commander of the palace guard infantry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
Shi Hongzhao was made military governor of Xu Prefecture and commander of the palace guard infantry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
許州 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), distinct from 徐州 Xuzhou; the original conflates the two.

On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, Chengyou great general of the Left Guard, and Chengxun the third son great general of the Right Guard; Lady Song of Pengcheng was created Princess Yongning, and the nephew Chengyun was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard.

On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, the second son Chengyou great general of the Left Guard, and the third son Chengxun great general of the Right Guard; Lady Song of Pengcheng was created Princess Yongning, and the nephew Chengyun was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard.

The Chinese names three sons in order (承訓, 承祐, 承勛); the original drops “second son” and makes the third son look like another Chengxun of 承訓. The proposed wording restores birth order. Untoned pinyin for 承勛 remains Chengxun, matching the chapter’s name field.
When Mouhan arrived he killed the former Chunzhou governor Pan Huan in Luoyang.
When Mouhan arrived he killed the former Chanzhou governor Pan Huan in Luoyang.
前澶州節度使 is former military governor of Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.
When Mouhan arrived he killed Pan Huan, former military governor of Chunzhou, at Luoyang.
When Mouhan arrived he killed Pan Huan, former military governor of Chanzhou, at Luoyang.
The literal office title likewise misromanizes 澶州.
On jiaxu Wang Shouen was made Acting Grand Marshal and the former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao was made military governor of Chunzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
On jiaxu Wang Shouen was made Acting Grand Marshal and the former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
慕容彥超 was appointed 澶州節度使; Chanzhou, not Chunzhou.

On the day jiaxu Wang Shouen, military governor of Luzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former Prefect of Dizhou, was made military governor of Chunzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.

On the day jiaxu Wang Shouen, military governor of Luzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former Prefect of Dizhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
The literal appointment line has the same 澶州 romanization error.
